chapter: Ellington's later years and Quincy Jones
title: Ellington denied the mass media and the Pulitzer Prize
summary: Jackson and Hinton note Ellington never had a TV show or the Pulitzer despite honors; Duke said they didn't want him too famous too young.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Except when you look at the annals of America and commercialism, that in all the annals of Duke Ellington, all the songs he wrote, he never really had a television show and a guy like Lawrence Welk had one for 24 years, you know.
Well, there goes that thing again, you know, that keep you in your place still, regardless, you know.
-- a man like this, even in his death, he's been honored with so many great honors and so many doctorates, but to the mass media -- I mean, we eulogize great people.
Oh, yes. Do you remember they wouldn't give him the Pulitzer Prize, and he deserved it if anybody did.
So he answered them beautifully. He said, you know, he said, "I don't think they want me to become too famous too young." And how old was he then?
Oh, man, I loved this man.
